# Lab 1 - published checks (Tier A)

These are the checks `itsmlab verify 1` runs; the grader runs the same checker on the receipted
commit. Bundles: **Core** is pass/fail as a whole (every Core spec must pass; L1-CORE-5 is checked
by the grader and shown as `skip` locally), **Stretch** passes at any two of three, and the
reasoning in `DECISIONS.md` is read by the lecturer. Ids are stable.

Fixture calls (creating and driving tickets into the state a check needs) are not checks: when a
fixture call fails, every check that depends on it is reported as `error` with the fixture's
request and response in the message. Every request carries `X-Test-Clock`; T1, T2, ... refer to
the test vectors in `API.md` §4. "either" means both values are accepted and the one observed is
recorded for L1-CORE-4. Fixtures: 2.42, 2.43 and 2.45 share one T2 ticket that is never
acknowledged; 2.44 uses a fresh T2 ticket; every state-machine check uses fresh tickets driven by
fixture calls with clocks that may be earlier or later than clocks used by previous checks.

Limits: `docker compose --profile tests build` (every image, the `tests` one included, is built up
front; a tests image that does not build costs S3, never Core) is untimed in Tier A and killed after
300 s in Tier B (its job has 15 minutes); `docker compose up --wait svcdesk` and `GET /health` have
120 s; every HTTP request has 10 s; `docker compose --profile tests run --rm --build tests` (S3) has
300 s in both tiers, after which it is killed and S3 fails. Every input the checker sends is
deterministic and published (the titles, the reporter, the clocks T1..T7, the header on every
request): the checks establish conformance on these inputs, nothing more, and that is accepted by
design; the lecturer's human pass reads the code and `DECISIONS.md`.

## L1-CORE-1 `compose-up` (core)

| id | check | expected |
|---|---|---|
| L1-CORE-1.01 | compose file defines service svcdesk with build | a compose file exists at the repo root (discovery order `compose.yaml`, `compose.yml`, `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.yaml`, the first found wins, plus the matching `*.override.*` file if present) and defines a service `svcdesk` with a `build:` key (an `image:`-only service fails) |
| L1-CORE-1.02 | no host-path bind mounts | in the resolved configuration (`docker compose config --format json` over the same file list used for `up`) no service volume has `type: bind` and no top-level volume uses `driver_opts` with `type: none` or `o` containing `bind`; named volumes and `tmpfs` are fine |
| L1-CORE-1.03 | compose up --wait svcdesk within 120 s | after an untimed `docker compose build`, `docker compose up --wait svcdesk` succeeds within 120 s |
| L1-CORE-1.04 | GET /health answers 200 within 120 s | `GET /health` answers 200 within the same 120 s window |

## Advisory `ai-disclosure` (reported, not graded)

Every file under `src/` and `specs/` with extension .py .go .ts .js .java .cs .rb .rs .kt .md, plus `DECISIONS.md`, carries in its first ten lines a comment matching `ai-generated:\s*\d{1,3}\s*%\s*-\s*\S`; the report lists the files without it. Example header: `# ai-generated: 80% - Claude Code drafted, I rewrote the SLA clock`.
